description: Errors found by the parser: the tokens are not arranged according to the C/C++ grammar.

rules.title: Missing semicolon
rules.what: A statement is not finished: C/C++ needs a semicolon `;` at the end of every statement and declaration.
why: The `;` at the end of the line was forgotten.
The compiler only notices when it reads the NEXT token, so it often reports the line AFTER the real mistake.
fix: Add `;` at the end of line {real_line}.
rules.tip: Lines that do NOT get a semicolon: #include/#define lines, function headers like `int main()`, and lines ending with `{` or `}` of if/for/while blocks.

rules.title: Missing closing brace }
patterns: ^expected declaration or statement at end of input$
rules.what: A `{` was opened but never closed, so the compiler reached the end of the file still waiting for a `}`.
why: A block of an if / for / while / function was not closed.
Every `{` needs exactly one matching `}`.
fix: Add the missing `}` at the end of the block.
rules.tip: Indent your code consistently (4 spaces per block): a missing brace then becomes easy to spot because the closing braces no longer line up.
samples: expected declaration or statement at end of input

rules.title: Extra closing brace }
rules.what: There is one `}` too many. It closes a block (or the whole function) earlier than you intended.
why: An extra `}` was typed, or a `{` is missing at the start of a block.
fix: Remove the extra `}` on line {real_line}.

rules.title: Missing closing bracket )
rules.what: A `(` was opened but not closed with `)` before {before}.
why: A `)` was forgotten, often in an if/while condition or a function call with nested brackets.
fix: Count the brackets on line {line}: every `(` needs a matching `)`.

rules.title: else without a matching if
rules.what: The compiler found an `else` that does not belong to any `if`.
why: A semicolon right after the condition, `if (x > 0);`, ends the if-statement immediately.
The if-part has two or more statements but no `{ }`, so only the first one belongs to the if.
fix: Remove the `;` after `if (...)`.
Put the statements of the if-part inside `{ }`.

rules.title: Commas instead of semicolons in a for loop
rules.what: The three parts of a `for` loop must be separated by SEMICOLONS: `for (start; condition; update)`. Line {line} uses commas.
why: Commas and semicolons look similar, but inside `for ( )` the parts are separated by `;`.
fix: Replace the separating commas with semicolons.

rules.title: Missing ; after struct / class definition
patterns: ^two or more data types in declaration specifiers$
^new types may not be defined in a return type$
rules.what: A `{kind}` definition must end with `};` - the semicolon after the closing brace is missing (line {real_line}).
why: Unlike functions, struct/class/union/enum definitions are declarations, so they end with a semicolon.
fix: Write `};` instead of `}` at the end of the {kind} definition.

rules.title: Semicolon after a function header
rules.what: The function header on line {real_line} ends with a semicolon, so the `{ ... }` body below it is no longer attached to the function.
why: `int main();` is a declaration only. A function DEFINITION has no `;` between `)` and `{`.
fix: Remove the `;` at the end of line {real_line}.

rules.title: Code outside of any function
patterns: ^expected constructor, destructor, or type conversion before (?P<before>.+)$
rules.what: Line {line} is an executable statement, but it is outside of every function. Statements like calls, assignments, if/for/while and return must be inside a function such as `main()`.
why: The code was written above `main()` or below its closing `}`.
An extra `}` closed `main` too early, pushing the following lines outside.
fix: Move the statement inside `main()` (between its `{` and `}`).
samples: expected declaration specifiers or '...' before string constant

rules.title: Unknown type name or missing semicolon
rules.what: The parser was reading a declaration on line {line} and got confused before {before}.
why: The type name is misspelled or unknown (e.g. `Int`, `integer`, `String`).
The previous declaration is missing its `;`.
fix: Check the type name at the start of line {line}.
Check the end of the previous line for a missing `;`.

rules.title: A value is missing (expected expression)
rules.what: At this point the parser needed a value (a variable, number or calculation) but found {before}.
why: Something is missing after an operator or `=` (for example `int x = ;`).
Empty brackets where a condition or argument is required.
fix: Complete the expression on line {line}.

rules.title: A name was expected
rules.what: The parser expected a name (identifier) here but found {before}.
why: A keyword or number was used as a variable name (names cannot be keywords like `int`, `return`, or start with a digit).
Code is in a place where only declarations are allowed.
fix: Use a valid name: letters, digits and `_`, not starting with a digit, and not a keyword.

rules.title: do-while loop without while
rules.what: A `do { ... }` loop must end with `while (condition);` - it is missing after the closing `}`.
why: The `while (...)` part of the do-while loop was forgotten or misplaced.
fix: Add `while (condition);` right after the `}` of the do block.

rules.title: Function body without opening {
patterns: ^old-style parameter declarations in prototyped function definition$
rules.what: The function header on line {real_line} is not followed by `{`, so the statements below it are not inside the function body.
why: The opening `{` after `int main()` (or another function header) was forgotten.
fix: Add `{` at the end of line {real_line} (or on the next line).
samples: expected function body after function declarator

rules.title: case label without colon
rules.what: A `case` or `default` label must end with a colon `:`.
why: A semicolon or nothing was written instead of `:` (e.g. `case 1;`).
fix: Write `case 1:` (colon, not semicolon).

rules.title: Missing ] in array brackets
rules.what: An array index or size opened with `[` was not closed with `]`.
why: The `]` was forgotten, or something unexpected (like a `;` from a #define) appeared inside the brackets.
fix: Close the brackets: `a[5]`, `a[i]`.

rules.title: Condition without brackets
rules.what: In C/C++ the condition of `if`, `while`, `for` and `switch` must be inside brackets `( )`.
why: Python-style or pseudo-code style `if x > 5` was used.
fix: Put the condition in brackets: `if (x > 5)`.

rules.title: Missing opening brace {
rules.what: The compiler expected a `{` to start a block or a class/struct body here.
why: The opening brace of a function, class or struct was forgotten.
fix: Add `{` where the body starts.

rules.title: Syntax error: something is missing
rules.what: The parser expected {expected} at line {line}, column {col}, but found something else. Something just before this position is missing or in the wrong order.
why: A missing symbol such as `;`, `)`, `}` or `,`.
An extra or misplaced word.
fix: Look at line {line} around column {col}, and at the end of the line before it.

rules.title: case / default outside a switch
patterns: ^case label not within a switch statement$
^'default' label not within a switch statement$
rules.what: A `case` or `default` label appears outside of a `switch { ... }` block.
why: The `switch (...) {` line is missing, or its block was closed too early by an extra `}`.
fix: Put all case labels inside the braces of a `switch (variable) { ... }`.
samples: case label not within a switch statement

rules.title: Label with nothing after it
rules.what: A `case`/`default` label (or goto label) is the last thing in a block, with no statement after it.
why: `default:` was written at the end of a switch with nothing after it.
fix: Add a statement after the label, e.g. `default: break;`.
samples: label at end of compound statement

rules.title: Array size written with ( ) instead of [ ]
patterns: ^expected declaration specifiers or '\.\.\.' before numeric constant$
rules.what: Line {line} declares an array with round brackets `( )`. Array sizes go in SQUARE brackets `[ ]`.
why: `( )` and `[ ]` mixed up - round brackets are for functions, square brackets are for arrays.
fix: Write `int a[5];` instead of `int a(5);`.
samples: expected declaration specifiers or '...' before numeric constant
